territorial_scope.description: Applies to data controllers and processors subject to Kenyan regulations and, under regulation 26(3), reaches controllers processing personal data outside Kenya when the Cabinet Secretary requires compliance with regulation 26(1).

evidence.quote: the Cabinet Secretary may require a data controller who processes personal data outside Kenya to comply with subregulation (1)

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Kenya's Data Protection (General) Regulations 2021 (Legal Notice 263 of 2021) are made under the Data Protection Act and set duties for data controllers and processors on consent, data subject requests, retention, processor contracts, automated decisions, impact assessments, breach notification and cross-border transfers, commenced 14 January 2022.
summary.long: Legal Notice 263 of 2021 sets detailed rules under Kenya's Data Protection Act. It was published and commenced on 14 January 2022 and is shown as revised to 31 December 2022. It applies to data controllers and data processors, except civil registration entities covered by separate regulations. Operative provisions cover consent and lawful bases; data subject requests (restriction, objection, access, rectification, portability, erasure) with fixed response periods; direct-marketing rules with an opt-out, and a fine of up to twenty thousand shillings or six months' imprisonment for unlawful commercial use; retention schedules and processor contracts; in-country storage for specified state-interest processing; data protection by design; breach notification to the Data Commissioner; transfers abroad based on safeguards, adequacy, necessity or consent; prior impact assessments for listed high-risk processing, including automated decisions and biometric data; and exemptions for national security by Cabinet Secretary certificate and for public-interest situations.

notes: Text is the Kenya Law consolidation as revised by the 24th Annual Supplement (Legal Notice 221 of 2023) as of 31 December 2022. Published in Kenya Gazette 14 January 2022 and commenced that day; the registry title uses 2021. The Act is the enabling statute and the Regulations implement it section by section. Relations to other Kenyan instruments are as listed, but the Kenya Law metadata lists 'Is amended by 24th Annual Supplement', which is not recorded as an amendment relation here. Internal inconsistencies and drafting problems: reg 11(4) refers to a fee 'charged under subregulation (2)' though reg 11(2) concerns only the form; reg 43(1) refers to contractual binding corporate rules 'contemplated under regulation 41', which does not mention them; reg 52 refers to an 'Assessment Report' under section 23 of the Act without defining it; reg 45(1) and reg 41(1) contain drafting errors ('is such a transfer is necessary', 'to a another country').

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in the operative provisions changes legal treatment. The numbers present are procedural time limits (fourteen, seven, thirty and sixty days in regs 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 18, 51 and 52), which are events rather than thresholds, and the fine and imprisonment maxima in reg 15(4), which are enforcement. Reg 49 sets high-risk DPIA triggers without numeric cutoffs (e.g., 'large scale'), and the child-related provisions (regs 13 and 22 and Part VIII) do not fix an age. The Second Schedule lists notifiable data categories without monetary or numeric thresholds.
